guidelines.detail: refines FID-01 (The description explicitly says that the picked items undergo quality control, and the reference places that activity between picking and subsequent work. The generated model has no counterpart for the check, so this is an omission rather than an alternative element choice. This guideline refines the general instruction to model every distinct activity by specifying how to model checks on the resu)

same as LRN-028 (The generated start and end labels express the described trigger and outcome, while the matched reference labels are generic. The other label pairs are close paraphrases; the clearest supported guidance is to retain meaningful boundary-event labels.)

same as LRN-005 (The records show sequence flows missing where the description states an order or conditional transition, including the start-to-first-activity flow. This is essentially the learned guideline LRN-005, with the start-event case made explicit.)

refines FID-03 (The description says the customer reports issues, while the generated label recasts this as receiving a report. Preserving the stated actor and action makes the label more faithful. This refines the documented advice to use short, faithful labels; LRN-012 also supports preserving stated actions, but does not specify preserving the actor’s perspective.)
same as LRN-005 (The records describe ordered actions and conditional paths whose sequence flows are absent. This guideline is essentially the same as learned guideline LRN-005.)

same as LRN-028 (The description identifies the process trigger and the payment-failure outcome, while the reference uses generic start and end labels. The evidence supports meaningful boundary labels; it does not support making labels generic merely to match the reference.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names multiple activities that must all occur and another activity that occurs only in certain cases as part of the same stage: Model the required activities and the conditional activity so synchronization waits for all required work but only for conditional branches that were activated; use an inclusive split and join rather than a parallel join that waits for every possible branch.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that one or more activities occur only when a condition holds, alongside required activities that must be completed before a later step.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a check or inspection is carried out on the result of an activity: model the check or inspection as a distinct task after that activity and before the next described work
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a check or inspection is carried out on the result of an activity

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states what initiates the process or identifies the outcome at which it ends: Label the corresponding start or end event with a concise phrase that faithfully names that stated boundary, rather than a generic label or a related intermediate activity.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description identifies what initiates the process or states an outcome at which it ends

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description presents distinct activities in an ordered progression, including transitions into, through, or out of branches or synchronization points: Connect each consecutive activity with a sequence flow, preserving the stated transitions through branches and synchronization points.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description presents distinct activities in an ordered progression, including transitions into, through, or out of branches or synchronization points, or identifies an action that initiates the process

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description attributes an action that prompts further work to a specific actor: Label the corresponding activity with that actor performing the stated action, rather than recasting it from the perspective of another participant receiving or handling it.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description attributes an action that prompts further work to a specific actor
